topic: Someone finds their grandmother's engagement ring in a pawn shop
text: I held the ring tightly, its cool metal a whisper of mornings long past, of hands that shook with joy when it first slipped onto a finger. In the worn pawn shop, among forgotten things, it lay as if waiting, and I knew it was for me to find, to weave back into the tapestry of memories where it belonged. The weight of it in my palm spoke of stories yet to be told, of connections mended. I would bring it home, not just an object, but a link, a bridge back to the smiles and the sunlight of days when promises were new.
